### Home Field usability audit — a deliberate divergence is a gap only where its substitute is missing, weaker or undiscoverable

`verified` · `@legeos.assessment.home-field-usability-gaps-20260831/1` · scope `path "apps/**"`, `path "compositor/**"`, `path "portals/**"`, `path "services/lege-filed/**"`, `path "shell/**"`

Audited the Home Field and the modules around it against mainstream desktop expectations. The Home Field's rejections — no taskbar, no tray, no virtual desktops, no title bars — are the product, so this audit judges each one by its substitute rather than by the convention it dropped, and reports a gap only where the substitute is missing, weaker or undiscoverable. On that test the shell's own rejections mostly hold; what fails is a different class of thing entirely — capabilities the project intends to have, believes it has, or documents as shipped, which are absent in code.

JUDGED BY SUBSTITUTE, AND SOUND. Virtual desktops: rejected by the one-workspace invariant (compositor/COMPOSITOR.md:12); substitute is park-to-tile plus show-all plus Alt-Tab; the substitute is real, but window.park has no chord at all and window.show-all has no pointer route outside one context menu, so the gap is discoverability, not the missing workspaces. Taskbar: rejected; substitute is the field's own app and parked-session tiles, which is a genuine replacement. Tray: rejected under the services-not-indicators constraint; substitute is the widget system plus ProviderRole slots, which works for network via the user's nm-tray2 but leaves a third-party app no place to dock. Title bars: no server-side chrome renderer, so decoration is forced client-side (compositor/lege-comp/src/xdg_shell.rs:467); the substitute for close is a context-menu row and for resize a compositor-painted grip, but there is no user-facing maximize control at all — a window only maximizes if the app asks.

GENUINE GAPS, RANKED BY DAILY COST. (1) No multi-select anywhere: the field carries a single focus: Option<TileId> (shell/lege-shell/src/surface/field_screen.rs:157) and the drawer browser a single entry_focus: usize (surface/file_browser.rs:54); no shift-click, ctrl-click or marquee exists, so no bulk action on files or tiles is possible. (2) Nothing is discoverable: no cheat sheet, tooltip, help overlay or first-run anywhere in the shell; park, close, restore and reset have no chord and live only in a right-click menu the user must guess is there; the action manifest can already generate a cheat sheet and nothing renders one. (3) No file operations from Home: navigate and open only — no rename, copy, move, new folder, properties or clipboard, and no drag of a file into an application; Operation::OpenWith and AddReference return None (field_screen.rs:1435). (4) The trash could not list its contents. (5) Accessibility is claimed but not built.

DOCUMENTED-BUT-ABSENT, which is a distinct and worse category than merely missing, because the docs assert it: docs/architecture/accessibility.md claims AT-SPI support and a high-contrast variant for every shell surface; no atspi dependency exists in any Cargo.toml and no contrast token or theme exists in shell/lege-shell/src. a11y.seed installs Orca with nothing to read, because the shell paints itself with a custom rasterizer and exposes no accessible name, role or state for any tile, row or widget. Reduced motion and the focus ring are real and respected; the rest of the claim is not implemented.

ABSENT WITH NO SUBSTITUTE: Lifecycle1.Lock hard-fails NotSupported although the compositor fully implements ext-session-lock-v1 — nothing drives it; volume, brightness and battery exist nowhere in the tree as code, not as stubs; the Files app has no new folder, search, sort control, view mode or breadcrumbs, though lege-filed supports CreateDirectory; the OpenURI, Screenshot, ScreenCast and Print portals do not exist; no removable-media mount or eject; no display configuration; no keyboard-layout switcher, touchpad settings or IME.

STALE LEDGER CLAIMS corrected by this audit: the graphical settings app and the shell's notification rendering both shipped on 2026-08-30, after the 08-27 readiness audit that called them stubs, and the portal NoUiAvailable path is now a headless-only fallback rather than the default.

### Home vision and daily-development usability review

`verified` · `@legeos.assessment.home-vision-review-20260905/1`

Reviewed Home against @legeos.work.home-surface-usability-next, the representation-ladder decision, the application-only launcher decision and hands-on run 5. Source inspection and deterministic renders support the core shape: one bounded field with stable user-directed geometry, explicit folder/project/window-group containers, an application-only launcher, one Settings object and Home occlusion beneath application windows. The pinned Files application in the visual fixture is an explicit pin, not evidence that automatic app duplicates returned. This review does not establish real-seat composition, hardware input or mixed-scale acceptance.

Concrete defects repaired at this commit: (1) context menus clamped their background but continued painting and hit-testing rows off-screen; the menu now pages and scrolls within its bounds, including keyboard wrap to the last action and two-press close confirmation. (2) Files ground had no terminal route and the row verb demanded one selected item; ground now targets the current directory independently of selection. (3) Copy/Cut existed as toolbar/keyboard verbs but were missing from the row menu. (4) Help compressed busy categories into overlapping rows; readable fixed-height rows now scroll, including keyboard navigation, with Close remaining outside the viewport. (5) folder request failures were removed from the cache and rendered forever as reading; the error is now retained and shown while the existing refresh beat can recover. (6) parent navigation retained the child scroll offset and truncated-list captions overpainted the last row; both are corrected.

Remaining existing-scope priorities: folder windows still use a separate minimal listing (paint_folder_window), with immediate file opening, no row selection or full file context menu, no hidden-file toggle and no sort/view controls. Their existing three-second BrowseDirectory refresh is not integration with index change signals. The richer Files object supports many of these verbs, but it is not yet a shared per-folder browsing surface. Carry its state and actions into folder windows rather than inventing another file-operation implementation. The action gate still exempts pointer routes for group cycling and terminal toggle, as the existing application-integration and window-group records already acknowledge. These are implementation gaps within the existing vision, not requests to adopt a conventional taskbar or a new workspace model.

The mostly-empty cold Home layout remains an unresolved product choice. Filling all space would conflict with stable placement and useful drop space. Two extrapolations are proposed separately, with no code implementation: @legeos.work.home-developer-setup-preview (an opt-in preview of a developer working set) and @legeos.work.home-project-development-status (service-backed, explicit project build/test status with freshness). Neither authorizes background repository commands, automatic project inference or live repacking.

### Homegarden usability review: synchronize the view, protect manual layout, and make garden controls honor their labels

`verified` · `@legeos.assessment.homegarden-usability-review-20260908/1`

Review of the Homegarden addition at fbe44804 against @legeos.decision.homegarden-activity-grown-places and the active Phases 0-3 work. Judged by the agreed substitute and its promises, not by demanding a conventional desktop. Nielsen's visibility of system status, user control/freedom, consistency and recognition heuristics provide the secondary UI lens. No production code or live desktop was changed. The installed-session/day-long gates remain open.

P1 — HOME DOES NOT FOLLOW RESIZE/REMOVE. shell/lege-shell/src/surface/app.rs:662 adopt_remote_tiles only inserts IDs absent locally; DataUpdate::FieldRemote at 1164 routes every HomeField1.Changed fetch through it. Garden tending depends on that signal for all field changes (1893-1904). Thus growth, shrink, hiding and recession can be persisted while the current shell retains old sizes/tiles. Reconcile authoritative remote document changes with outstanding local operations and revisions; verify one complete Observe -> Tend -> Changed -> draw journey.

P1 — MANUAL OWNERSHIP IS NOT PROTECTED. services/lege-sessiond/src/apis/homegarden.rs:193 recognizes a manual size only when tended_span already exists and differs; new contexts have tended_span=None. Garden and manual folders intentionally share the same path ID. A manually placed 3x3 folder therefore becomes eligible for Trace resizing to 2x2 when first observed. Moved tiles only update landing and never acquire a protection flag. The Remove branch in crates/lege-field/src/garden.rs:94 checks pinned alone, so even a known user-sized tile can disappear when Dormant. PlacedOnHome's protective observation is explicitly deferred, but the adopted no-touch promise is already active. Track provenance and explicit user ownership at placement/move/resize boundaries; preserve it for growth, yielding and recession.

P1 — RESIZE CAN MOVE ANOTHER PLACE. crates/lege-field/src/garden.rs:160 approves reflow.moved by ownership/pin/user_span only, without checking position. reflow.rs:265 yielded_placement changes the neighbor's near edge (and hence cell). In an in-memory fixture, growing A from 2x2 to 3x2 shifts neighboring B from column 2 to 3. Emitting no Move opcode does not establish stable positions. Reject automatic reflows that change any surviving Place's cell, or explicitly reconcile the invariant with a different spatial-anchor definition. Current property tests start with manually seeded app tiles and new contexts, so they do not exercise existing garden neighbors through growth.

P2 — GARDEN CONTROLS DO NOT HONOR THEIR LABELS. 'Keep this size and place' is mapped to exactly Pin(true) (shell/lege-shell/src/garden.rs:150); pin neither captures user_span nor blocks own growth. 'Remove from Home' calls Forget, which only erases the ledger context (services/lege-sessiond/src/apis/homegarden.rs:468); the tender iterates remaining contexts, so the tile is orphaned instead of removed. ForgetAll has the same orphaning behavior. Hide sets hidden without clearing pin, while the tender refuses to remove pinned contexts, so a pinned Place stays. These are independent of the shell synchronization bug. Make keep preserve the actual span, explicit removal remove the tile and appropriate ledger state atomically, and explicit hide work on pinned Places with a visible recovery path. Reversibility must cover garden state as well as field state where the action promises it.

P2 — DEFAULT LANDING PREVENTS THE BRANCH RUNG. The default bottom-left 2x2 Trace sits flush against the grid bottom (garden.rs HomeCorner::cell). find_resize anchors at top-left, so on a 12x8 field the (0,6) tile can reach only 4x2 when Expanded requests 4x3. The Folder Large floor is 9 cells, so 4x2 remains Wide and paint_place never reaches the branch body. Reserve vertical growth room or introduce a deliberate growth-anchor policy consistent with spatial memory; do not silently move the tile. The first bottom row of traces is affected even with ample space above.

P2 — DEFAULT-ON AUTOMATION HAS NO GRAPHICAL SETTINGS ENTRY. The schema defines shell.home-garden.* including enabled, corner and ignore, but apps/lege-settings/src/surface.rs:1526 page_for admits only shell.home-field.* and shell.appearance.*. No garden controls reach the form. Add a concise Homegarden section with on/off, excluded folders, and recovery of hidden places, leaving tuning parameters secondary.

SECONDARY UI REFINEMENT. MenuTarget carries a folder path but no garden membership or pin state: ordinary folders including Desktop receive Pin/Unpin/Keep/Hide/Why rows even when HomeGarden1 does not know the path; both Pin and Unpin appear simultaneously. Tailor rows to actual state, retain provider tools for every folder, and keep only distinct commands. Explain automatic presence concisely and keep details inspectable: Why currently uses a transient notice with roughly 324px of message area and a CTRL+Z hint, which is a poor container for a long causal explanation. Do not restore the retired Home plate/Help button to solve discoverability.

VALIDATION LIMITS. The 16 existing ledger/tender tests pass. Seven standalone in-memory probes reproduce the model behaviors above, recorded in @legeos.evidence.homegarden-usability-review-20260908. Shell synchronization and settings/menu routing were traced statically. No pixel/a11y/hardware pass was claimed: offscreen.rs and the FieldScreen harness supply garden: HashMap::new(), so current baseline renders do not exercise a real Place. Growth forms/materials/facets, broader activity sources, threshold tuning and the Desktop choice remain the explicitly deferred design work, not new defects asserted by this review.

### Hot-fixability and daily-development readiness, 2026-08-31

`verified` · `@legeos.assessment.hotfixability-current-state-20260831/2` · scope `path "crates/lege-state/**"`, `path "debian/**"`, `path "distro/**"`, `path "docs/planning/**"`, `path "installer/**"`, `path "packaging/**"`, `path "scripts/reinstall-legeos-desktop.sh"`, `path "services/lege-hostd/**"`, `path "session/units/**"`

LegeOS is currently suitable for active development as an additional desktop session on a stable Ubuntu host with the host session, display manager, TTY and backups retained as recovery paths. Stage-1 packages can be installed while the old session runs; applications, shell and separated services provide progressively restartable activation boundaries, while the compositor honestly requires logout and kernel/driver/boot changes require a staged reboot. It is not yet suitable as the sole recoverable bare-metal daily driver because installer/ISO and clean-install gates are unfinished, boot-deployment rollback is not hardware-proven and ADR-0004 remains open, coordinated service restart and cross-version state/IPC skew are unproven, and the archive path is inconsistent with the Rust 1.97 workspace and still has sibling path dependencies.

**depends_on** `@legeos.decision.compositor-on-smithay/1`, `@legeos.work.desktop-validation-foundations/1` · **supersedes** `@legeos.assessment.hotfixability-current-state-20260831/1` · **derived_from** `@legeos.assessment.desktop-test-readiness-20260827/1`

### Eighteen unsatisfied command acceptance checks run in one sweep; all pass

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.acceptance-sweep-20260904/1`

Every acceptance check whose method is `command` and which had no evidence was run on this host, in one pass. Not passing, each for a stated reason rather than a defect in what it tests: image-consumes-closure needs mkosi, which is not installed (exit 127); metapackages-built fails because the eight metapackages are not built yet AND because `lege dev repo verify` cannot read the archive keyring as a non-root user; closure-report runs and exits zero but resolves nothing, because no machine here has Ubuntu 26.04 indexes, so it stays inconclusive rather than satisfied. nested-session-journey failed and was fixed rather than excused: see @legeos.observation.two-daemons-opening-one-fresh-state-db-raced-its-migrations.

### baseline + btrfs delta equals a fresh direct scan, field for field, on the fifth fixture run

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.btrfs-delta-correctness-gate-passes/1`

Run by the user as root against the loopback Btrfs fixture on 2026-09-04. All five harness tests pass in 352 s. The gate is that an index carried forward only by decoded btrfs send --no-data streams equals an index built from nothing against the final tree, compared field for field on path, kind, size, alloc, mtime, ctime, mode, hidden, dev, inode and nlink; a third arm carried forward by today's reconcile is compared too, as a check on the harness itself. It holds across 24 scenario/tree-size rows (1,540 / 15,339 / 153,327 entries; nothing at all, 100 new files, an hour of desktop use, a 5,000-file build burst, a whole-directory rename, a mass delete, one 1 GiB file, truncate-chmod-rewrite-in-place). The edge-case round trip covering hard links, symlinks, a whole-directory rename, a rename cycle and a move onto an occupied path reports planned_paths 10, mutations 11, creates 3, removes 1, moves 5, touches 2 — exactly what the in-tree test encoder predicted before the fixture confirmed it. An interrupted delta is refused rather than half-applied at all 64 truncated prefixes of a 7,360-byte stream. This was the fifth run: four earlier ones failed, each on a real bug (@legeos.observation.a-send-stream-names-paths-relative-to-the-subvolume-not-the-index-root, @legeos.observation.a-directory-whose-contents-changed-kept-a-stale-modification-time).

**Verifies**

- `completed` `@legeos.work.adaptive-index-maintenance/1` — check `measured-backend-choices`

### The user reviewed the behaviour change in session and delegated the call, saying they did not see what choice there was to make and trusted the judgement. Accepted: the emergency kill delay is now a property of the selected victim's instance identity rather than of the Critical episode. What changes is that a newly selected victim always gets the full checkpoint deadline before KillCgroup, so a long Critical episode whose victim keeps changing can terminate nothing for as long as the ranking keeps moving; what it removes is a victim being asked to checkpoint and killed on the same tick, having inherited an already-expired countdown. The governor stays observe-only under @legeos.constraint.identity-and-launch-safety, so the change is proven by replay, not on the live machine, and no user data was ever at risk from either behaviour.

### Home clears its whole buffer, so the bar's strip keeps nothing from a taller frame

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.home-clears-the-bar-strip-20260907/1`

The row of widget controls in the bar's strip was stale pixels, not a stray placement. Home's buffer is never cleared between frames and FieldScreen::draw filled only `area`; `app.rs::redraw_home` insets by BAR_HEIGHT only while `self.bar.is_some()`, and the bar is created after the bridge connects, so the first frames run the full height of the output and lay tiles down to it — after which nothing ever wrote to the last 48 rows again. `ui.painter.clear` replaces the partial fill. The new test draws one taller frame then one inset frame into the same buffer and fails without the fix with 24606 stale pixels, the first at (377, 800) in 0x00d5dae0 — the tile edge colour measured at the box borders in Lane 1's screenshot. 355 lege-shell tests pass.

**Verifies**

### The idle index watcher went from 121 wakeups per minute to none, measured against a binary built from the pre-fix commit

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.idle-index-wakeups-eliminated-20260904/1` · scope `path "services/lege-filed/src/watcher.rs"`, `path "tools/xtask/src/index_bench.rs"`

Over a 60 second settled idle window with one armed fixture root, the pre-fix binary (built from a git worktree at the parent of commit 6522e10, so this is a true before/after rather than a recollection) recorded 121 timeslices and 120 voluntary context switches; after the fix both are 0. read_bytes, syscw and wchar were already 0 on this workload in both builds, so the gain is wakeups and the roots-table write per tick, not read I/O. Measured from /proc/<tid>/schedstat and /proc/<pid>/status for the lege-index-watcher thread. The harness had to be an xtask subcommand rather than a benches/ target, because watch::guard panics on any real watch root when the executable path contains a deps component, which is true of every cargo bench and integration-test binary; this was verified directly rather than assumed. Four defects in the harness itself were found and fixed during the run: a wrong schedstat field index, per-task versus per-process voluntary_ctxt_switches, a pid-matching bug against a leaked process, and the sandbox-specific discovery that File::set_modified raises no inotify event here while touch(1) does.

### M1: a trial boot can fail because the session never came up

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-boot-health-can-fail/1`

lege-sessiond reports session health to lege-hostd at the moment it signals systemd readiness, so an absent session-healthy marker now means the session did not come up rather than that nobody could report it. The compositor-active marker stays deliberately unwired and reports Skipped, because sessiond has no honest evidence for it; the two switches are separate so arming one never arms the other. A skip never arms a reboot, and only a boot genuinely trialling a candidate can force one.

### M1: the checkpoint protocol is deliverable end to end, and verifies its peer

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.m1-checkpoint-transport/1`

org.legeos.Checkpoint1 is served by an application instance and called by lege-sessiond on the governor's behalf, addressed by a bus name derived from the InstanceId so nothing is registered and no directory goes stale. The daemon resolves the claimed name's PID and confirms its cgroup names that exact instance before believing any answer — an application squatting another instance's name is refused without being called — and every call is bounded by the request's own deadline, so a peer barely responsive under the pressure that prompted the request is refused rather than hanging the relay.

Every service-absent path degrades to one sentence naming the service, verified with no bus present. Toolkit-dependent choosers are explicit seam traits that refuse rather than fabricate.

### nm-tray-2 is pinned, declared in the session layer, and builds as legeos-nm-tray

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.nm-tray-2-packaged-20260904/1`

Both gates pass. The fork is pinned in distro/forks/manifest.toml with package = legeos-nm-tray; distro/seeds/selection.toml names it in the session layer with role network-control; the generated legeos-desktop and legeos-session-full control files both depend on it. Packaging lives at distro/forks/nm-tray-2/debian/ so the package's name, dependencies and install paths are LegeOS facts that check-packaging can see, while the source stays unvendored (ADR-0005). scripts/build-fork-deb.sh produced legeos-nm-tray 0.5.1+legeos1~g0965344 from the user's checkout: /usr/bin/nm-tray, /usr/share/applications/nm-tray.desktop (the name shell/lege-shell/src/surface/app.rs resolves when nothing declares org.legeos.NetworkTray), /etc/xdg/autostart/nm-tray-autostart.desktop, translations, Provides/Conflicts/Replaces nm-tray, and nothing under /usr/local. One thing is NOT satisfied and the build refuses rather than hides it: --popup, the session-bus forwarding slot and the X-LegeOS-* desktop keys exist only in an uncommitted working tree and are absent from every pushed commit, so a package built from the pin would install, resolve as the network provider, and do nothing when clicked. distro/forks/nm-tray-2/preflight.sh fails the build on that, and the pin cannot be trusted until those changes are pushed.

The four tests that carry this work: sleep_signals_become_session_edges (a stream of logind
booleans becomes Sleeping(true)/Sleeping(false) on a subscriber - the match rule around it needs
a system bus and a machine willing to suspend, so pump_sleep is split out as the part a test can
reach); only_the_shell_may_report_an_unlock (an unidentifiable caller and an application unit
are both refused with AccessDenied, lege-shell.service is accepted and the edge arrives);
an_observer_is_told_the_resolved_id_and_the_arguments; and both_launch_paths_report_to_the_observer,
which is a source assertion rather than a live launch because a real launch shells out to
systemd-run --user and no fake backend exists - what it protects is a launch path growing that
forgets to report, which would fail silently and for ever.

interfaces/baseline.json (the baseline was re-frozen with the coordinator's unfinished

actually fire on real hardware - a real lid close, a real unlock - and that busctl calling

requires limited.is_none() and unreadable_dirs == 0 and unwatched_dirs == 0 (commit f6e8961).
trash-undo-reported-a-restore-it-did-not-perform — Step::MoveToTrash{trashed} and
Step::RestoreFromTrash{restored_to} record the executed paths and undo_of reads them back
(services/lege-filed/src/operations.rs:848-868). the-provisioner-wrote-no-fstab-at-all —
installer/provision.sh:586-621 writes /etc/fstab by UUID.
a-snapshot-did-not-say-which-change-position-it-was-consistent-with — SnapshotManifest
carries snapshot_seq (crates/lege-file-index/src/snapshot.rs:106,134,205).
a-send-stream-names-paths-relative-to-the-subvolume-not-the-index-root — DeltaTarget carries
subvolume_path and root_path separately with a component-bounded containment check
(btrfs_delta.rs:961-968,1166). fresh-store-wal-switch-races-without-a-busy-handler — the WAL
pragma retries through retry_while_locked for 5s (crates/lege-state/src/lib.rs:92-114).
two-daemons-opening-one-fresh-state-db-raced-its-migrations — migration runs under BEGIN
IMMEDIATE with the applied-check repeated inside the transaction (lib.rs:227).
index-change-signals-never-fire — main.rs:228-230 installs Index1Signals as the change sink
and it captures a runtime Handle (index_host.rs:383,388).
deployments-subvolume-not-declared-by-repart — 10-root.conf:11 declares
Subvolumes=/@ /@home /@var /@snapshots /@deployments. hands-on-run-4-findings-20260903 —
every diagnosed cause addressed: ProtectHome=yes gone from lege-hostd.service, the Wayland
socket is literally wayland-0 (compositor/lege-comp/src/main.rs:67) so snapd's AppArmor
allowance matches, and /var/lib/snapd/desktop is in application_dirs()
(desktop_import.rs:48). home-hands-on-failures-diagnosed — SmolStr multi-character handling
fixed (surface/window.rs:105-117), XkbConfig::default() no longer used (state.rs:298), icon
resolution rate-limited per frame (app.rs:340), the inverted rung rule corrected so
session.poweroff is Large and session.logout Small (widgets/mod.rs:142-146), and Lifecycle1
registration is unconditional (sessiond main.rs:429,454).

WATCHES REMOVED, because the claim is time-invariant and no code change can falsify it: a
fixed-commit profiling result, a kernel or btrfs behaviour, or a fact about how Ubuntu 26.04
packages firmware. These had been going stale repeatedly for reasons unrelated to what they
claim. Their observed_at is deliberately left at the commit they were measured against,
which is what makes them meaningful, and each was given a review_after instead.

RE-OBSERVED at e6e1b1c3, still true: home-tree-exceeds-the-inotify-watch-budget
(WatchBudget::from_limits still halves max_user_watches, watch.rs:157);
home-refresh-costs-profiled-20260902 (audio.rs still spawns wpctl per Get, lifecycle.rs
Can* still calls logind uncached); openuri-is-the-frontends-portal (AssociationApi::new
still does not export mimeapps.list, crates/lege-associationd/src/dbus.rs:43-57);
the-nvidia-lrm-cannot-be-installed-in-an-unshared-bootstrap-chroot (distro/iso/build.sh:71-74
unchanged); release-debs-ship-unstripped-line-tables (Cargo.toml:139 still
debug = "line-tables-only", no separate-debug-symbols in any of the 13 deb blocks);
homegarden-produced-no-visible-place-or-bloom (garden::observe is still called only for
directory-opened and the path-bearing CLI launch; no Bloom implementation exists anywhere).
Two are partly fixed and re-observed on that basis: hands-on-run-20260831-findings (tile
drag-move and corner resize now exist with tests, the rest needs a hardware pass) and
hands-on-run-3-findings-20260903 (copy-path now really copies via copy_text_to_clipboard,
window minimize/close controls exist, resize covers full edge zones; band-over-client-content
remains deliberate design per COMPOSITOR.md).
this-machines-partition-table-cannot-hold-legeos-as-it-stands is likewise partly fixed: the
provisioner now has a --free-space mode that consumes a disk's free tail without zapping it
(commit 0627367), while the disk measurements themselves are hardware facts.

### The Fable advisor's round on the bottom-edge change: seven findings, all fixed

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.the-bottom-edge-reviewed-and-its-seven-findings/1`

Seven defects, six of them consequences of a screen-filling window's tag strip being drawn over its own client area where a framed window's is drawn beside it: the tag gap fell through to the window behind; every affordance press was delivered to the client as well; covering_chrome was filtered on read and so could never be cleared, bringing the strip back with no dwell on the next maximize; the peek band is the strip's own bottom ten pixels, so aiming at the close tag opened the switcher under it; a click nudged the window three pixels; the covering window was found without asking whether it was visible; and the machine cluster was destroyed with no home_revealed term and no way back. Two judgement calls taken from the same review: the peek enters the shell's own reveal rather than bypassing it, so one gesture has one way out; and the cluster returns on the peek. All seven fixed at 38b16d5, gate green, 1999 tests.

### A second adversarial review of the cluster split and the fullscreen chrome found eight issues; all eight were fixed. The gate is green after all of them.

### wl_data_device bound: selection out and in, drag-out, serial discipline; live-seat observation awaits the nested run

`verified` · `@legeos.evidence.wayland-clipboard-transport-20260831/1`

The record's whole intent landed: the compositor already served wl_data_device (Smithay handlers were wired all along; no compositor change needed), and the shell now binds the manager plus a second wl_seat on winit's connection purely for serials, offers both prepared targets (GNOME cut target first) with payloads captured at copy time, accepts foreign offers on paste by asking who owns the selection (bounded 250ms/4MiB synchronous read), exports drags edge-triggered on lift, and never invents a serial — with the Smithay finding recorded that set_selection is accepted by keyboard focus, which Home holds by construction. The Home browse surface also gained its Rename dialogue. Eleven fixture tests drive the decision rules and real-pipe transfers. Remaining, stated in code and in the agent report: drag-in from other applications, primary selection, and a shell-drawn drag icon; live-seat behaviour (paste into a GTK/Qt app, foreign copy into Home, drag-out onto another window, seat-binding coexistence with winit) awaits a nested-session run.
